name: AI Deep Dive — TSM — 2026-05-02
rationale: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) is the undisputed king of semiconductor foundries. Its near-absolute monopoly on leading-edge chip manufacturing (sub-5nm) gives it unparalleled pricing power, driving a 44.5% TTM net margin and a Rule of 40 score over 100. As AI demand necessitates ever-shrinking nodes from customers like Nvidia, AMD, and Apple, TSMC's structural dominance is only increasing. Even applying conservative multiples relative to its fabless peers, the stock is deeply undervalued. Our base case DCF suggests a fair value of $671.68, offering 68.9% upside from current levels. BUY.

bear.rationale: Growth decelerates to 15% as non-AI segments remain sluggish. Net margin compresses slightly to 40% due to the heavy depreciation burden of new fabs in the US and Japan. The exit P/E compresses to 20x, reflecting significant geopolitical risk discounts. The 1.1x quality multiplier acknowledges the geopolitical risk weighing on an otherwise perfect business moat.
risks: Severe cyclical downturn in consumer electronics offsets AI growth
Geopolitical escalation around Taiwan suppresses the valuation multiple

base.rationale: Growth of 25% represents a conservative deceleration from current 35% growth, reflecting sustained AI silicon demand. Net margin expands to 45% as N3 and N2 nodes achieve high yields and strong pricing power. The exit P/E of 25x is justified for a company with monopolistic pricing power in an essential industry. A quality multiplier of 1.20x is applied due to their undisputed technological lead over Intel and Samsung.
risks: Delays in ramping up N2 (2nm) nodes
Concentration risk with top clients like Apple and Nvidia

bull.rationale: Catalyst: AI and Custom Silicon demand trigger an unprecedented supercycle, leading to chronic undersupply of leading-edge wafers and immense pricing leverage. Revenue sustains a 32% CAGR. Massive operating leverage pushes net margins to 48%. The market awards a 30x exit P/E, re-rating TSM closer to its fabless peers (NVDA, AMD). The 1.25x quality multiplier reflects an absolute, unassailable monopoly on global computing progress.
risks: High multiples make the stock vulnerable to any minor earnings misses

analyticsLog.shareCountMethod: Used 5.186B (shares_diluted). Matches API output for the ADR.
analyticsLog.marginAnchor: TTM 44.5% used. Margins are incredibly robust and stable despite heavy capex (39.4% -> 40.0% -> 44.5%), reflecting immense pricing power on leading-edge nodes.
analyticsLog.growthDerivation: Analyst Y1 revenue implies ~35% growth. Given the insatiable demand for AI chips from Nvidia and AMD, we apply a hypergrowth deceleration model but maintain a high base case of 25% 5-yr CAGR due to multi-year visibility in leading-edge fab bookings.
analyticsLog.sectorBenchmarkRow: Technology — Semiconductors / Foundries: median P/E 20, best-in-class 30+. Used 25x for base case, acknowledging a slight geopolitical discount on an otherwise perfect business.
dataQualityFlags: Revenue API data was supplied in TWD while price was in USD. We converted raw TWD metrics (revenue/income) by an exchange rate of 32.5 to reflect pure USD fundamentals.
analyticsLog.confidenceBreakdown: 0.90/1.0 — +0.10 for pristine financial metrics (Piotroski 9, high margins, massive FCF), -0.10 for ever-present geopolitical overhang from China-Taiwan relations.
